title: Cost-Optimized Architectures
oneLiner: Deliver the same outcome for less: right pricing models, storage tiers, and cost visibility.
examWeightNote: Design Cost-Optimized Architectures (20% of the exam) — your final domain.
objectives: Choose EC2 purchasing options: On-Demand, Reserved Instances, Savings Plans, and Spot.
Use S3 storage classes and lifecycle policies to cut storage cost.
Right-size and use auto scaling / serverless to avoid paying for idle capacity.
Gain cost visibility with Cost Explorer, Budgets, and the Cost and Usage Report.

services.name: EC2 Pricing Models
services.purpose: On-Demand (flexible), Reserved/Savings Plans (commit for discount), Spot (deep discount, interruptible).

services.name: S3 Storage Classes
services.purpose: Standard, Standard-IA, One Zone-IA, Intelligent-Tiering, Glacier tiers — trade access speed for cost.

services.name: S3 Lifecycle Policies
services.purpose: Automatically transition or expire objects to cheaper tiers over time.

services.name: AWS Cost Explorer & Budgets
services.purpose: Visualize spend and set alerts when costs or usage exceed thresholds.

services.name: AWS Compute Optimizer / Trusted Advisor
services.purpose: Recommend right-sizing and flag idle or underutilized resources.

keyConcepts: Use Spot Instances for fault-tolerant, interruptible workloads (batch, CI, big data) to save up to ~90%; use Savings Plans/Reserved Instances for steady, predictable usage.
S3 Intelligent-Tiering automatically moves objects between access tiers based on usage — good when access patterns are unknown or changing.
Lifecycle rules transition infrequently accessed data to IA/Glacier and expire old data, cutting cost without app changes.
Avoid paying for idle: right-size instances, use Auto Scaling to match demand, and prefer serverless (Lambda, Fargate) for spiky workloads.
Set AWS Budgets alerts and review Cost Explorer / Cost and Usage Report and Trusted Advisor recommendations regularly.

scenarios.scenario: A nightly batch job processes large datasets and can safely restart if interrupted. The team wants the lowest possible compute cost.
scenarios.question: Which EC2 purchasing option is most cost-effective for this workload?
scenarios.explanation: Spot Instances offer up to ~90% savings and are ideal for interruption-tolerant, restartable batch work. Reserved/On-Demand cost more; you'd reserve capacity only for steady, always-on workloads.

scenarios.scenario: Log files are read frequently for 30 days, rarely after that, and must be retained for 7 years for compliance. The team wants to minimize storage cost automatically.
scenarios.question: What is the best approach?

options.label: Keep everything in S3 Standard forever
Use an S3 Lifecycle policy: Standard → Standard-IA → Glacier, expiring after 7 years
Store the logs on a large EBS volume

scenarios.explanation: A lifecycle policy transitions objects to cheaper tiers as access drops (Standard → Standard-IA → Glacier) and expires them at 7 years, minimizing cost while meeting retention — no application changes required.

quiz.question: Which EC2 pricing model offers the deepest discount but can be interrupted with little notice?
quiz.explanation: Spot uses spare capacity for up to ~90% off but can be reclaimed by AWS, so it suits fault-tolerant, interruptible workloads.

quiz.question: You have unpredictable S3 access patterns and want automatic cost savings without manual tuning. Which storage class fits?
quiz.explanation: Intelligent-Tiering automatically moves objects between frequent and infrequent access tiers based on usage, optimizing cost when access patterns are unknown or changing.

quiz.question: Which tool lets you set a threshold and get alerted when your AWS spend exceeds it?
quiz.explanation: AWS Budgets tracks cost/usage against thresholds and sends alerts. Cost Explorer visualizes trends; the Cost and Usage Report gives the most granular data.

quiz.question: Which is a recommended way to avoid paying for idle compute capacity?
options: Run all workloads on the largest instance type
Use Auto Scaling and serverless to match capacity to demand
Provision for peak load at all times
quiz.answer: Use Auto Scaling and serverless to match capacity to demand
quiz.explanation: Matching capacity to demand with Auto Scaling and serverless (Lambda/Fargate) means you don't pay for idle resources — a core cost-optimization practice.

quiz.question: For a steady, predictable workload running 24/7 for the next year, which option gives the best discount over On-Demand?
quiz.explanation: Committing to consistent usage with Savings Plans or Reserved Instances (1- or 3-year terms) yields significant discounts for steady workloads. Spot suits interruptible work, not always-on production.

quiz.question: Which S3 storage class offers the lowest cost for rarely accessed, long-term archival data where retrieval of hours is acceptable?
quiz.explanation: Glacier Deep Archive is the lowest-cost class for long-term archives accessed very rarely, with retrieval times measured in hours — ideal for compliance archives.

quiz.question: Which service provides recommendations to right-size EC2 instances based on utilization?
quiz.explanation: AWS Compute Optimizer analyzes utilization metrics and recommends right-sizing for EC2, Auto Scaling groups, EBS, and Lambda. Trusted Advisor also flags idle/underutilized resources.

quiz.question: How can you automatically move older S3 objects to cheaper storage classes without changing your application?
options: Configure S3 Lifecycle policies to transition and expire objects
quiz.answer: Configure S3 Lifecycle policies to transition and expire objects
quiz.explanation: Lifecycle rules automatically transition objects to cheaper tiers (e.g. Standard-IA, Glacier) and expire them on a schedule — cost savings with no application changes.

quiz.question: Which purchasing option is best for short-term, unpredictable workloads that cannot tolerate interruption and don't justify a commitment?
quiz.explanation: On-Demand has no commitment and no interruption risk, making it ideal for short-term, spiky, or unpredictable workloads. Spot is cheaper but interruptible; RIs/Savings Plans need commitment.
